deviations.reason: google/uuid accepts arbitrary outer bytes at length 38; Hirsel requires braces. uuid-rs agrees with Hirsel.
deviations.spec:
`bits` holds the 16 bytes most significant first, so comparing `bits` orders
version 7 UUIDs by time. `parse` accepts, as Go google/uuid and uuid-rs, the
hyphenated form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`, the same in braces or
after `urn:uuid:` in any case, and 32 bare hex digits, in either case; the byte
length selects the form, so any other length is `Length(n)` and the first
character that does not fit is `Char(offset)`. `to_string` and `@format` write
the lowercase hyphenated form. `version` is the top four bits of byte 6 and
`variant` the top bits of byte 8, whatever their values; `unix_ms` is the
48-bit timestamp of a version 7 UUID of the RFC 9562 variant.

deviations.reason: Upstream error text and indices are retained raw. Hirsel length-first and first invalid byte diagnostics are expected from each deliberately positioned mutation, not translated from observed Hirsel results.

deviations.reason: Rust builders take fixed-size arrays and truncate timestamps; Hirsel returns None for other lengths or millis >= 2^48.
deviations.spec:
`v4_from` stamps the version 4 and variant bits onto 16 bytes, keeping the other
122. `v7_from` puts a millisecond Unix timestamp below 2^48 in the top 48 bits
and 10 bytes below it, the version replacing the first byte's top four bits and
the variant the third byte's top two, as uuid-rs
`Builder::from_unix_timestamp_millis`; other lengths or a larger timestamp are
`None()`. `v4` draws 16 bytes from `Random` and `v7` reads the wall clock,
rounding its nanoseconds down to milliseconds, then draws 10 bytes; a reading
before 1970 is `BeforeEpoch()`. No state is kept between calls, so two version 7
UUIDs of one millisecond are unordered (RFC 9562 section 6.2 makes the counter
optional).

deviations.reason: Fixed scripted reads; negative wall and errors return before random. No ambient sources, counter or monotonic ordering requirement.

deviations.core_clock:
`clock.monotonic` samples an `Instant` of its clock. Its `instant.ticks` are nanoseconds
since an origin fixed for the run (`clock.monotonic.ns@1`), and later samples never
decrease. `instant.checked_add(clock, start, n)` advances an `Instant of clock` by `n`
nanoseconds, or returns `None()` when the ticks would pass `u64` MAX; it reads no clock
and records nothing. `clock.wall` returns signed Unix nanoseconds. A failed sample returns
`Unavailable()`, or `OutOfRange()` when the reading does not fit.
deviations.core_random:
`random.bytes(r, count)` returns exactly `count` bytes from the run's Random provider,
or `Unavailable()` with no bytes; it never publishes a partial draw. A zero count returns
empty `Bytes` without consulting the provider. A draw is nonblocking, like clock sampling,
so it is not a cancellation point ([CONC-3](concurrency.md#conc-3-cancellation)), and each
draw is a recorded capability input. The provider is chosen at launch
([providers](determinism.md#run-configuration)): `random.splitmix64@1` is a deterministic
simulation, predictable from the run's Random seed, and never protects a secret;
`random.system@1` reads the host's cryptographically secure generator.

observation: Every row compares raw u128 bits, canonical lowercase text, version, variant and unix_ms. Successful pure rows also check to_bytes/from_bytes and @format. Provider tapes enforce exact request order/count and short-circuit failures; same completion bytes reach every engine. Normal source/V check and runtime/tool failures are failed obligations.
input_hash_format: SHA256 of the UTF-8 canonical JSON input object (sorted keys, compact separators); text values encode the exact UTF-8 parser bytes; random_hex supplies exact provider bytes.
output_projection: pipe-separated raw u128 decimal, canonical lowercase spelling, raw version nibble, variant ordinal (Ncs=0/Rfc9562=1/Microsoft=2/Future=3), optional millisecond timestamp; upstream RFC4122/NCS names are renamed to the public Hirsel variant names.
